Aperture turns the camera hole into a small live island for the things you care about, in your phone\'s own colors.

Only an accessibility service can draw over the status bar, where your camera is. Aperture uses it for that alone, plus knowing which app is in front so the island can step aside. It can\'t read your screen.\n\nIn the next screen, open Aperture island and switch it on.

Notification access is how Aperture learns about your music, timers, deliveries and calls. It only looks at them to show them, and keeps nothing.\n\nIn the next screen, allow Aperture media and notifications.
Choose which apps can appear on the island. The usual ones, like YouTube Music, Spotify, WhatsApp and Clock, are already on.

Android brings Aperture back by itself when your phone restarts. So that a battery saver never stops it, let it run in the background: in the next screen, tap App battery usage, then Allow background usage, and choose Unrestricted. You can change this any time.
Play some music, then leave the app. The island will be waiting around your camera.

Opens your email app with a message to the developer. It includes a device report (phone model, Android version, the island\'s measurements and your Aperture settings) so the problem can be fixed; you can read and edit it before sending. Nothing is sent unless you press send.
Pausing hides the island and keeps your settings. Uninstalling removes Aperture and everything it stored, including its permissions. No questions asked.
The island is paused. Switch it back on any time.
What happened, and what did you expect? (The device report below helps fix it. Remove anything you don\'t want to share.)
Force-stopping Aperture (or a battery tool doing it) switches its accessibility permission off, and Android doesn\'t turn it back on. Open Aperture: the red step shows what to re-enable.
Android shows its own heads-up too. For apps you follow on the island, turn off Settings, Notifications, the app, Pop on screen.
Music is playing but nothing shows.
The island hides while the player app is open. Leave the app. Also check the app is switched on in step 3.
It stopped working after I turned on Advanced Protection.
Android 17 Advanced Protection blocks every accessibility service that isn\'t an accessibility tool, including every island app. Turn Advanced Protection off to use Aperture.
What does Aperture know about me?
Only what is on your notifications and media sessions, while it shows them. It has no internet permission, stores nothing but its settings, and never reads your screen.

After the pill shrinks, a thin ring around the camera keeps showing what\'s live: song progress, a timer\'s seconds, a delivery\'s progress. Green means a call is in progress. Paused music shows no ring. Tap the ring to open it again.
Fine-tuning for people who like to tinker. The defaults are chosen to be right for most people.
Only these apps can appear on the island. Suggested apps are on to start with.
Off. Turn on "Aperture island" in Accessibility.

Advanced Protection is on. Android blocks accessibility services that are not accessibility tools, so the island cannot draw until you turn Advanced Protection off. This is a system rule and no island app can work around it.

What the accessibility permission is used for: drawing the island over the status bar, and knowing which app is in front so the island hides in camera apps. Aperture cannot read screen content, has no internet permission, and keeps nothing off your phone.

Black: pure OLED black. Glass: translucent, your wallpaper shows through. Clear: more see-through. Art: the album cover, blurred. Tonal: your theme\'s surface color. The small pill always stays black so it blends with the camera.
Shows sample activities on the island without any app.
This is how a message from WhatsApp will look. Swipe up to dismiss.
Try it out on the island
The outline shows the camera cutout Android reports. Nudge the ring until it sits evenly around your camera. Changes apply live.
This notification can no longer be replied to.

Aperture uses the Accessibility API for two things only:

• To draw the island above the status bar, around your camera. Only an accessibility service can draw there.
• To know which app is in front, so the island can step aside in camera apps and while you are in the app it is showing.

Aperture does not read, collect or store what is on your screen or what you type. It has no internet permission, and nothing is shared with anyone.

Tap Agree, then turn on Aperture island in the next screen.
